literal: Happiness without interruption will accumulate, desire which is called among sufferings the suffering if destroyed.
translation: If desire, which is the greatest suffering of all sufferings, is destroyed, uninterrupted happiness will crowd in.
modern: துன்பங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் பெரும் துன்பம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஆசை அழிந்துவிட்டால், இடைவிடாத இன்பம் வந்து பெருகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that desire is not just one of many problems, but the ultimate source of misery, described here as the 'suffering of sufferings' (துன்பத்துள் துன்பம்). When this root cause of pain is completely eliminated, true happiness (இன்பம்) naturally rushes in without any gap or interruption (இடையறாது). The word 'ஈண்டும்' beautifully suggests that joy will crowd in and fill the space once occupied by craving. Thus, the eradication of desire is presented as the single key to experiencing continuous, everlasting peace.
